response.overview: Murder in Paris (aka Paris Efter Midnight aka French Life) was the second of five burlesque shorts presented in anaglyphic 3-D by Oakland and San Francisco burlesque theater magnate, Harry A. Farros.  Photographed in Los Angeles circa May 1953, the title was changed to Parisienne Life shortly before releases in September 1953.  It's likely that while working with George Weiss at Screen Classics in the spring of 1953, Edward D. Wood Jr wrote the script for this 3-D short. While it is not listed on his resume, it was photographed on the same day as Cleopatra Follies (aka Flame of Islam) which Wood does list as a writer's credit.
response.title: Parisienne Life
